description: Sen. Ron Johnson of Wisconsin (R) discusses the rising cost of US involvement in Iran, the outlook for defense spending and potential supplemental funding, the ongoing DHS funding standoff, and the path forward for the SAVE America Act. Senator Johnson speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Sen. Ron Johnson on Iran Costs, DHS Funding, SAVE Act
Oil Jumps as Iran and Israel Trade Strikes on Energy Facilities

description: Joseph Lavorgna, SMBC Americas Chief Economist, states “they did what they were suppose to do” when sharing his thoughts on the Federal Reserve opting to keep interest rates steady. He also talks about the potential economic risks from higher prices in gas and oil, and discusses how long he thinks the US economy can withstand these prices. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg’s “Balance of Power.” (Source: Bloomberg)
title: The Fed Did What They Were Suppose To Do: Lavorgna

author: Fiona MacDonald
description: Kuwait announced the second arrests this week involving a group that it said was affiliated with Hezbollah, adding that it had foiled a plot to target vital facilities in the Gulf state.
title: Kuwait Says More Suspects Linked to Hezbollah Have Been Arrested

author: Daniela Milanese
description: Brazil is sending humanitarian aid to Cuba as the island faces a deepening economic crisis under increasing pressure from the Donald Trump administration.
title: Brazil Sends Food, Medicine to Cuba as Crisis Deepens

author: Joe Mathieu, Kailey Leinz
description: Senator Ron Johnson, a Wisconsin Republican noted for his focus on curbing spending, defended President Donald Trump’s pursuit of the war against Iran ahead of a possible supplemental funding request.
title: GOP Senator Ron Johnson Backs War as Vital to Ending Iran Threat

description: Nadhim Zahawi, former UK Chancellor of the Exchequer, shares his thoughts on President Trump criticizing UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer for not being more supportive of the US’ efforts when it comes to Iran. He talks about whether or not the UK navy should get involved with securing the Strait of Hormuz, how the UK economy will be affected by higher oil prices, and why he changed political parties. Nadhim Zahawi speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Nadhim Zahawi on Iran, Oil & UK Economy

author: Zoe Tillman
description: The number of companies suing for tariff refunds has spiked in recent weeks, a sign that many importers aren’t confident yet in the Trump administration’s plans to create a claims process after the US Supreme Court struck down the president’s trade policies.
title: Tariff Refund Lawsuits Surge Amid Uncertainty About US Plans

author: Patpicha Tanakasempipat
description: Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul is poised to win lawmaker approval for a new term less than six weeks after elections, potentially bringing stability to the country’s often volatile political landscape and allowing him to manage the fallout from the war in the Middle East.
title: Thai Leader Anutin Set to Extend Rule in Vote After Election Win

author: Emily Birnbaum
description: Despite deep pockets, the two industries came away with just one victory.
title: Illinois Primary Contests Show AI, Crypto Money Isn’t Everything

author: Anthony Capaccio, Jen Judson
description: A top US army official said the service is “very close” to fielding the US military’s first hypersonic weapon, a forecast at odds with recent Pentagon assessments that more testing is needed before it should be deployed.
title: Army ‘Very Close’ To Fully Fielding First US Hypersonic Missile

author: Michael D McDonald
description: Costa Rica closed its embassy in Cuba citing attacks on free speech and a deteriorating economy that has made it difficult to find basic goods.
title: Costa Rica Closes Embassy in Cuba Citing Deteriorating Economy

author: Ellen Milligan
description: The UK’s political left is beginning to articulate an alternative to Starmerism as the governing Labour Party wrestles with its direction ahead of expected widespread losses in May’s local elections.
title: Starmer Rivals Make Play for Labour’s Disaffected Base in UK

description: Representatives for the financial services firm and the US Commerce secretary’s family declined to reveal the amount. An ethics expert said the loan may be ‘another favor his family owes Tether.’
title: As Lutnick Sold Cantor to His Children, Tether Gave Them a Loan

description: "Personally i believe he will stay on past the midterm elections," Bob Michele, JPMorgan Asset Management's global head of fixed income, says about Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell staying at the central bank. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Powell Will Stay on at the Fed, JPMorgan's Michele Says

description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz discuss the latest from the Middle East. On today's show, Democratic Congresswoman Haley Stevens, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino and CSIS Senior Fellow Clayton Seigle. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US Aims to Curb Soaring Oil Prices | Balance of Power: Editor Edition 3/18/2026

author: Anthony Capaccio
description: A new US intelligence assessment backed away from previous projections that China wants to be ready to retake Taiwan by force as early as next year, reflecting a broader push by the Trump administration to adopt a more conciliatory tone toward Beijing.
title: US Intelligence Agencies Soften Outlook on China’s Plans for Taiwan

author: Miles J. Herszenhorn
description: US supplies of key long-range and defensive munitions were already running low before the latest strikes on Iran, a constraint that may force Washington to scale back its role in the conflict, according to Seth G. Jones of the Center for Strategic and International Studies.
title: Expert Says US Iran Strikes May Last Only Days or Weeks Longer

author: Andra Timu, Irina Vilcu
description: Romanian lawmakers hit a deadlock in budget negotiations, potentially jeopardizing efforts to narrow a fiscal deficit that’s become the biggest in the European Union.
title: Romania’s 2026 Budget Hits Deadlock as Coalition Tensions Rise

description: Venezuela’s acting President Delcy Rodríguez ousted defense chief Vladimir Padrino in a sweeping shake-up of the armed forces.

description: The Canadian government has set aside C$1.4 billion ($1 billion) for domestic defense manufacturers to expand ammunition production.
title: Canada Earmarks $1 Billion to Boost Ammunition Production

author: Olga Tanas
description: Faster reform of the UK’s North Sea windfall tax could significantly cut reliance on LNG imports, the industry lobby group said, as war in the Middle East highlights energy supply vulnerabilities.
title: UK Oil, Gas Lobby Group Urges Tax Reform to Reduce LNG Imports

author: Kavita Mokha
description: President Emmanuel Macron on Wednesday named the nation’s next aircraft carrier “Free France,” in a homage to the World War II resistance movement as the nuclear power moves to bolster its naval capabilities.
title: Macron Names Next Flagship Aircraft Carrier ‘Free France’

author: Michael Nienaber
description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz called for Europe to more assertively pursue its interests in a global environment where the US under President Donald Trump and China dominate geopolitical power dynamics.
title: Merz Rallies for More Assertive Europe in Geopolitical Turmoil

author: Annmarie Hordern, Ari Natter
description: Vice President JD Vance and other key Trump administration officials plan to huddle with oil executives Thursday as the White House looks for ways to tame surging fuel prices after the US attack on Iran, according to people familiar with the matter.
title: Vance to Huddle With Oil Executives as Global Fuel Prices Spike

author: Daniela Milanese, Beatriz Reis
description: Brazil’s government announced new measures to enforce minimum freight rates for truck drivers, as a surge in fuel prices driven by the Middle East conflict rattles oil markets.
title: Brazil Acts to Avert Truckers Strike as Oil Surge Fuels Tensions

author: Anthony Halpin
description: Russia plans to provide naval convoys to protect merchant ships as it seeks to bolster the defense of the nation’s vessels and so-called shadow fleet.

description: Senator Rand Paul, a Republican, challenges fellow Republican Senator Markwayne Mullin, the nominee to lead the Department of Homeland Security, about his "anger issues." Paul questions if Mullin has the right temperament for the job during his confirmation hearing. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Paul Asks Sen. Mullin Why He Called Him a 'Snake'

description: Will Israel’s killing of Ali Larijani, a veteran Iranian politician known for his pragmatism, weaken the chance of a US exit strategy for the Iran war? Nicole Sy explores who could be left to run the country. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: After Larijani’s Killing, Who Else in Iran Can the US Talk To?

author: Jamie Tarabay, Anthony Capaccio
description: Spy chief Tulsi Gabbard dodged questions about the severity of the threat posed by Iran in Senate testimony on Wednesday, with the long-time skeptic of foreign interventions careful not to contradict either her own past beliefs or the Trump administration’s stance on the conflict.
title: Gabbard Dodges Questions on Whether Iran Was ‘Imminent Threat’

author: Emily Birnbaum, Yash Roy
description: Democratic voters in Illinois this week rejected most candidates supported by the crypto and artificial intelligence industries, marking an unexpected defeat for well-funded special interest groups as they prepare to spend hundreds of millions of dollars to shape Congress in this year’s midterm elections.
title: AI, Crypto Suffer Surprise Defeats in Illinois Primary Fights

description: Netanyahu may have won Trump over for the war in Iran, but he’s losing Americans in the process, Bloomberg Opinion columnist Ronald Brownstein says. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US Views on Israel Hit Striking Milestone

description: The Republican chairman overseeing hearings on Senator Markwayne Mullin’s nomination to lead the Department of Homeland Security challenged the Oklahoma Republican on whether his “anger issues” disqualified him from leading an agency enmeshed in controversy over aggressive tactics.
title: Rand Paul Challenges Trump DHS Pick Mullin on ‘Anger Issues’

description: In separate letters, Democrats Wyden and Whitehouse press the deputy attorney general and attorney general for answers on secret Epstein investigations involving transnational organized crime.

title: Trump Waives US Shipping Law For Oil and Gas In Bid to Lower Prices

description: The United Nations nuclear watchdog urged the US and Iran to resume negotiations, saying concern over Tehran’s nuclear program can’t be solved by military action alone.
title: UN Nuclear Watchdog Urges Return to Negotiations on Iran Program

title: Unblocking Strait of Hormuz Is in China’s Interest, Greer Says

description: Justices fast-tracked arguments on the president’s power to end protections for migrants fleeing violence after lower courts called out unexplained emergency rulings.
title: Pressure Grows for Supreme Court to End ‘Emergency’ Wins for Trump

title: India Sends Warships Near Gulf of Oman to Escort Its Fuel Ships

description: Iran said US and Israeli airstrikes hit its giant South Pars natural gas field and associated infrastructure, state TV reported.
title: Iran Says Strikes Hit Key South Pars Gas Field, Oil Facilities

author: Reinie Booysen
description: A prolonged conflict in the Middle East will heighten the risk of a “major economic downturn” and increased inflation, adding a new stress point in financial markets that were already under strain, Singapore’s President Tharman Shanmugaratnam wrote in a Facebook post.
title: Iran War Poses Risk of ‘Major’ Economic Downturn, Singapore President Says

author: Charlie Duxbury
description: The risk of an attack by the Iranian regime in Sweden has increased as a “desperate” Iran could become more dangerous under US and Israeli military pressure, the Nordic state’s security service said.
title: Sweden Sees Greater Domestic Threat From Iran as War Rages

author: Samuel Stolton
description: The European Union has unveiled a red-tape-cutting plan dubbed “EU Inc.” to boost the emergence of companies that could compete on the world stage with US and Chinese rivals.
title: Europe Unveils ‘EU Inc.’ Plan for Startups to Rival US, China

author: Mariana Durao, Daniel Carvalho, Mie Dahl
description: US efforts to forge a major critical minerals partnership with Brazil are stalling as the South American nation struggles to finalize its own plans for the sector and political tensions rise ahead of presidential elections later this year.
title: US Snubbed by Lula Government at Brazil Critical Minerals Summit

description: The Japanese leader is among the first from a country singled out by Trump to visit since the war began.

description: The North Atlantic Treaty Organization is deploying a second Patriot missile-defense system to Turkey’s Incirlik Air Base to bolster the alliance’s air defenses against threats from Iran.
title: NATO Boosts Defenses With Second Patriot Deployment to Turkey

author: Alex Wickham
description: China’s military has been studying President Donald Trump’s war on Iran for lessons that could prove helpful in any future conflict of its own, according to Western officials familiar with the matter, scrutinizing US offensive capabilities as it sees the strategic balance shifting in its favor in the Indo-Pacific.

description: Relatively fewer workers are paying in, while retirees are living longer. Something has to change.
title: Will I Get My Full Social Security Benefits? Definitely, Maybe

description: North Korea may have supplied weapons and troops worth as much as $14 billion to support Russia’s war in Ukraine, though only a portion of that appears to have been paid back to the reclusive regime, a study said.

description: Attia built his brand on trust and credibility. The revelation of a yearslong relationship with Jeffrey Epstein has upended that.

description: A year ago, Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard testified at the Senate’s annual hearing on global threats that Iran wasn’t building a nuclear weapon.
title: Gabbard Set to Face Scrutiny Over Iran Stance at Threats Hearing

description: Oil dipped as Iraq signed a deal to resume exports via Turkey that avoids the Strait of Hormuz, and as the US stepped up efforts to force the reopening of the key waterway. Iraq agreed with Kurdistan to resume oil exports through a pipeline in the semi-autonomous region that goes to Turkey’s Mediterranean port of Ceyhan. The rerouting of the oil will only partially relieve supply concerns. Bloomberg’s Anthony di Paola reports.
title: Oil Prices Drop as Iraq Signs Pipeline Export Deal

author: Julian Harris, Ellen Milligan
description: Britain’s resurgent Green Party will call on Prime Minister Keir Starmer to hike taxes on businesses and the wealthy in order to subsidize voters’ household bills, in light of soaring energy prices from the US war on Iran.
title: UK Greens Want Tax Rise on Oil, Wealth to Help Ease Energy Bills

description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said in a video statement earlier in the week that his military is "undermining this regime in the hope of giving the Iranian people a chance to remove it." Bloomberg's Dan Williams breaks down the situation. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Netanyahu: Undermining Regime so Iranians Can Remove It

description:
On today's show, oil pares gains as Iraq resumes crude exports through Turkey, avoiding the Strait of Hormuz. The reopening of the Ceyhan pipeline follows a deal with the semi-autonomous region of Kurdistan.

US President Donald Trump has given up on efforts to recruit partners to help secure the Strait of Hormuz and scolded allies who openly rejected his appeals. He described the reaction from NATO allies in particular as a "foolish mistake".

Bond traders are paring bets against Fed rate cuts this year ahead of today's decision, which is expected to be a hold. Investors await Chair Jerome Powell's comments on the impact of the Iran war in his penultimate press conference.

And Bloomberg understands that Unilever is considering splitting off its food assets. 

Today's guest: Dominik von Achten, Heidelberg Materials CEO (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran War: Iraq Exports Oil Via Turkey & Trump Gives Up On Hormuz Help | Daybreak Europe 3/18/2026

author: Brendan Scott
description: Angela Rayner, the former deputy prime minister who’s bookmakers’ favorite to succeed Keir Starmer as Labour leader, said the governing party is “running out of time” to deliver change, in her most public criticism yet of the premier’s leadership.
title: Rayner Says Labour ‘Running Out of Time’ in Critique of Starmer

description: Iranians set fire to US and Israel flags in Tehran on March 17. Source: Getty Images/Getty Images
title: Iran Strikes Continue After Larijani’s Killing Confirmed

description: Iran confirmed the death of Ali Larijani, the Islamic Republic’s national security chief and a key figure in its wartime leadership. This is after Israel announced that it had killed him in an overnight airstrike. Ryan Bohl, Senior Middle East and North Africa Analyst at RANE spoke to Bloomberg’s Horizons Middle East and Africa anchor Joumanna Bercetche on the likelihood of a diplomatic off ramp. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Bohl : Iran Running On Defensive Autopilot

author: Kateryna Kadabashy, Hadriana Lowenkron, Sherif Tarek
description: Iranian attacks on Israel and Arab states in the Persian Gulf continued overnight into Wednesday, while President Donald Trump said the US could end the war with the Islamic Republic “in the near future.”
title: Iran Vows Revenge for Larijani as Trump Says War May End Soon

description: US President Donald Trump abandoned his effort to recruit partners for the war with Iran and scolded allies who openly rejected his appeals. Germany, France, Canada, Greece and Norway are among those that have explicitly ruled out participating in the US-Israeli operations. Trump also called out Japan, Australia and South Korea in a social media post that stated the US didn’t need the help of anyone. Bloomberg’s Joumanna Bercetche breaks down the situation.
title: Trump Ditches Appeal for Help in Iran War

author: Bilal Hussain (News), Khalid Qayum
description: Pakistan’s deadly airstrikes in Afghanistan this week have sparked global alarm and calls for ceasefire, as the world grapples with the implications of another major conflict near Iran.
title: Pakistan’s Deadly Strikes in Kabul Prompt Calls for Ceasefire

author: Ben Westcott
description: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will travel to Australia next week, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced, just days after she said that a trade deal between the two sides is “in the final stretch.”
title: EU Commission Chief to Visit Australia as Trade Deal Approaches

author: Arne Delfs
description: Friedrich Merz, knee-to-knee in the Oval Office with Donald Trump, sat mute as the US president threw verbal darts at Spain, one of Germany’s European Union allies, complaining about its failure to help in the US-Israeli attack on Iran.
title: German Leader’s EU Frustration Is Getting More and More Obvious

author: Patpicha Tanakasempipat
description: Thailand’s Constitutional Court accepted a petition alleging that ballots cast in last month’s election may be traceable, a case that questions the validity of the poll and could disrupt the formation of a new government.
title: Thai Court Accepts Ballot Challenge, Risking Election Result

author: Sakura Murakami, Takashi Umekawa
description: A channeling of US resources into the conflict ravaging the Middle East could cause an imbalance in the current security environment surrounding Japan, renewing the need for the country to strengthen its defense capabilities, according to Japan’s former Defense Minister Gen Nakatani.
title: US Focus on Iran May Impact Asia, Japan’s Ex-Defense Chief Says

author: Shruti Singh, Miranda Davis, Bill Allison
description: Illinois Lieutenant Governor Juliana Stratton won the Democratic nomination for the state’s US Senate seat on Tuesday, beating a rival who far out-spent her and handing a victory to her boss and potential 2028 presidential candidate, Governor JB Pritzker.
title: Stratton Wins Illinois Senate Primary in Boost to Pritzker

author: Miranda Davis, Emily Birnbaum
description: Jesse Jackson Jr., a son of the late civil rights leader, fell short in his campaign to get reelected to Congress in the Illinois primaries after a race marked by heavy spending by both artificial intelligence and pro-Israel interest groups.
title: Jesse Jackson Jr.’s Comeback Bid for Congress Comes Up Short

author: Alastair Gale, Sakura Murakami
description: Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi faces a diplomatic balancing act at a summit this week with Donald Trump, after the US president called on Japan to deploy warships to help secure the war-stricken Strait of Hormuz — before abruptly dropping the demand.
title: Japan’s Takaichi to Face Trump After Allies’ Spat Over Warships

description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Former US Ambassador to Israel under the Biden administration Thomas Nides calls Iran’s regime “dangerous” and says he hopes the US and Israel are aligned in their objectives in the region. Port of Los Angeles Executive Director Gene Seroka says ship fuel costs have more than doubled in recent weeks amid disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. Representative Jim McGovern (D-MA) shares his reaction to President Trump claiming he'll have the honor of taking Cuba. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Counterterrorism Center Director Resigns Over Iran War | Balance of Power: Late Edition 03/17/2026

author: Magdalena Del Valle
description: Reductions in child mortality have slowed around the world and even stalled in some places, with communities in sub-Saharan Africa and southern Asia particularly at risk, a United Nations report has found.
title: Progress in Reducing Child Mortality Has Slowed, UN Report Finds
